LARRY progenitors travelling between states

Cells hop from measured cell to measured cell, steered by the scJDO2 drift (direction from lineage barcodes), so they always stay on real cells. They start in Undifferentiated and change colour as they move into a new state.

How this was made. 130,887 cells, 2,002 variable genes, a 10-dimensional latent space. Direction comes from lineage barcodes: each clone's centroid shift between its first and last time point, per unit time, given to all its cells. Clone velocity is not a gradient field, so the operator can be directional. On LARRY held-out clones, a walk on this kind of drift predicted clonal fate as well as a classifier trained on the fates (macro AUROC 0.89). scJDO2's MeasuredDrift is fitted to it on 25,624 cells (median cosine 0.84); the gene-level operator and archetypes are fitted on 2,000 cells sampled across states.

Walkers hop between measured cells. Each cell links to its 30 nearest cells in the latent space, and a hop to neighbour j is weighted by exp(cos(xj − xi, drift at i) / 0.25), the CellRank-style velocity kernel; about 150 hops per walker. 300 walkers start in Undifferentiated. At the end: Undifferentiated 12, Neutrophil 134, Monocyte 109, Baso 41, Mast 3, Meg 1. The floor is X_spring; the surface (valleys from cell density, slope from the projected drift) is a backdrop only. Playback counts hops, not time.

Held-out clone fate test. Clones split in half three times; settings chosen on training clones; scored on test clones' earliest cells against each clone's majority fate.
